we have developed a method that is able to reconstruct scenes from images taken from a large number of cameras that are far away from each other and that are widely distributed in the scene, and that we have shown how the method can be extended to handle images taken by cameras mounted on moving objects.
a new approach for photorealistic scene reconstruction is presented that is able to cope with large visibility changes and to produce a spatial and color reconstruction of the scene.

a novel scene reconstruction technique was presented, different from all previous approaches in its modeling of intrinsic color and texture information, and its ability to cope large changes in visibility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reconstructing a 3D environment from a set of images.
the reconstruction of the 3D structure of the scene and with the recovery of its color and texture properties from a set of images of the scene.

the following problems: (1) How to represent the 3D structure and appearance of an object in the scene, (2) How to reconstruct this information from a set of images of the scene, and (3) How to represent and manipulate this information.

the method presented is a novel, effective, efficient, and accurate scene reconstruction method, which can handle arbitrary scenes with large occlusions, and which can be applied with both inward-facing and outwards-facing cameras.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel scene reconstruction technique which is able to cope with large occlusions and changes in visibility, and which is able to model the scene's intrinsic color and texture information.
we have developed a novel approach for scene reconstruction that is able to deal with large variations in scene appearance and is robust to image correspondences.
we have demonstrated that the voxel coloring method is a viable approach for photorealistic 3D reconstruction from images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to reconstruct a photorealistic scene model from a set of images, even when the camera poses are not known and the scene is complex.
a single, simple and efficient scene representation can be used to reconstruct a large and complex environment, even when the cameras are far apart and widely dispersed.
the voxel coloring approach is capable of producing accurate scene reconstructions from images with very large changes in visibility.
